findings.reason: the plan needs a third arm where the measurement is possible and a waiver is stated, so an added failure is still charged and the waiver is not applied.
findings.text: s19's done-when tests a stated waiver only in the arm where the primary measurement is impossible, so an implementation that honours any stated waiver before attempting the measurement passes every arm (cases one and two carry no waiver, the waiver arm needs impossibility) while discarding the measurement the section exists to make; the deliverable's precedence — honoured only "when the primary measurement cannot be made" — is never measured

findings.reason: a fixture refused under an older tree revision whose promotion code is unchanged, which must stay refused, is what distinguishes a code-scoped comparison from a tree-scoped one.
findings.text: s20's fixtures differ in both the tree revision a verdict names and the content of the promotion code (older revision against current revision), so an implementation comparing the service's whole-tree revision with the primary head passes both; the primary branch moves on every landing, so under that reading every refusal is stale within minutes and "a refusal under current code is terminal as today" (plan.html:172) is never true

findings.reason: the waiver rule needs its own section and its own negative control, or s19's declared goal and gate describe only half of what a node would ship.
findings.text: s19 carries two independent deliverables: leaving head-only test files out of the primary measurement, and honouring a waiver when the measurement cannot be made; the waiver rule is wider than the section's title and evidence (it would pass any run with an impossible primary measurement, whether or not it adds a test file), and the single gate verdict proves neither half on its own
